home.title: Everyday output in one line. The monster when you need it.
home.lede: ConsoleMonster makes the output of the commands you already run readable, and draws tables, trees, charts, live runs, dashboards, menus and forms when you need more. One engine for .NET and PowerShell 5.1 and 7, with no package dependencies and plain lines when the output is a log.

items.title: Everyday
items.line: Better output for the commands you already run: one line turns it on for the session.
items.note: Shows PowerShell's own output, then the same commands after Enable-ConsoleFormatting and Get-Service grouped by status; it rests on the after view. Before and After under the player jump to each half. Recorded on PowerShell 7 from the script in the tab beside it.

code.label: PowerShell
code.text:
Import-Module ConsoleMonster
Enable-ConsoleFormatting

# Keep it on in every session: prints the lines for your profile.
Enable-ConsoleFormatting -ProfileSnippet

items.title: Monster

items.note: A whole console application, recorded from the Release build as it drives itself: a preset in the Shell menu, a form whose servers load for the chosen domain, the review with the equivalent command, the live dashboard, and the results with next steps. twins.title: One engine for C# and PowerShell
twins.body: The module's cmdlets are a thin layer over the same .NET library. Both programs shown here ran for this page, the C# in-process and the script on Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7 in a 92-column console. The site tool compared every cell they drew.

tiers.title: Readable on every console
tiers.body: ConsoleMonster detects the colour depth and which glyphs the console font can draw, and every widget renders at each level. Status never depends on colour alone: without colour, the symbol and the word remain.
points: Full, Basic and ASCII glyph sets; on conhost the font decides
NO_COLOR and the CONSOLEMONSTER_COLOR, _GLYPHS, _MODE and _THEME overrides

fit.title: Tables that fit the window
fit.body: Tables negotiate their width instead of overflowing it. This is the table above at 44 columns: below 60 cells, when the columns no longer fit, each row becomes a card titled with its key.
points: Columns hide by priority, and a footer names the hidden ones
Text wraps after separators, so paths and DNS names break where you would break them
A single record renders as a record view

live.title: Live dashboards from many threads
live.body: A live session takes updates from any thread through a lock-free queue and draws about 15 frames a second, writing only the cells that changed. Console output and PowerShell streams are captured into a log region instead of tearing the screen.
live.source: The stress test in ConsoleMonster.Examples: 32 workers, with stray Console.WriteLine calls. Figures from the ConsoleMonster 2.0 pull request.

live.stressNote: Recorded from a real run in a 120×40 pseudo console. The session drew 15 frames a second; this replay samples {fps} of them per second to keep the file small.

stress.title: The stress test
stress.body: 32 workers post lane updates as fast as they can while four threads write to Console.Out and Console.Error at random. The workers never touch the console: the session coalesces everything into about 15 frames a second and captures the stray output into the log region.
stress.source: Measured by the stress test itself during the recording above (.NET 8, Release build). The ConsoleMonster 2.0 pull request reports the same picture: 15.0 fps sustained at about 80,000 updates/s, 0 dropped, about 0.75 ms per frame.

assessment.title: Recorded once, replayed exactly
assessment.body: The assessment showcase does not run any rules. It replays a JSON-lines event stream of {events} events into a dashboard definition that knows nothing about the recording: every update arrives as a LiveEvent addressed by name.
assessment.recordBody: LiveRecorder writes one JSON object per applied event: the time in milliseconds, the target, the operation, the key and the values. LiveRecordingReader reads it back with no dependencies. Live sessions record with RecordPath or RecordWriter, and Start-ConsoleDashboard with -RecordPath.
assessment.layoutBody: Phases, lanes for twelve targets, a stacked bar and a key/value list, a braille line chart, a histogram, a bar chart and a log region. Below 60×20 the dashboard shows one status line plus the phases and the lanes that fit.

pipeline.title: A build pipeline, from C# and PowerShell
pipeline.body: A module build: phases, steps with timings, module facts, overall progress and the tool output. The C# showcase writes to Console.Out like a real tool, and the PowerShell script calls Write-Host and Write-Warning from the dashboard's runspace; both land in the log region. Each run was recorded in a 110×32 pseudo console.
pipeline.afterBody: When the session ends the screen is restored and a summary is printed to the scrollback, so a live dashboard always leaves a record behind. This is the C# run's summary.

stream.title: The same run in CI
stream.body: With CONSOLEMONSTER_MODE=stream, with redirected output or when a CI system is detected, a live dashboard narrates append-only lines instead of redrawing. This is the assessment replay at six times speed in stream mode.

query.title: Printed once: query results
query.body: Not every tool needs a live view. The DNS and mail-security showcase prints a summary, the records, a delegation tree, mail-security checks and resolver latency once, at the width of the console.

powershell.lede: {cmdlets} cmdlets with a plain Console noun, in one binary module for Windows PowerShell 5.1 and PowerShell 7. Every frame on this page was captured from both hosts running the script beside it.

format.title: Format-ConsoleTable beside Format-Table
format.body: The same four objects, formatted by the built-in cmdlet and by ConsoleMonster in a 100-column console. Format-ConsoleTable takes pipeline input and -Property as Format-Table does: names, wildcards and calculated properties, plus hashtables with column options.
points: Presenters for bytes, durations, dates, booleans and status
Without -Property, an object's DefaultDisplayPropertySet is used
Redirected output is plain text; -PassThru also writes the input objects

lists.title: Lists and trees
lists.body: Format-ConsoleList shows one object as a record view. Format-ConsoleTree -AsInspector walks nested objects and collections, with depth, item and node limits.

frame.title: The cost of a frame
frame.body: ConsoleMonster.Benchmarks builds a stress-sized dashboard (32 lanes, statistics, a sparkline and a log) at 140×45, applies 5,000 updates between frames and measures 600 frames: composing the frame, diffing it against the previous one and encoding VT, the characters written and the memory allocated. A live session does this work on one thread about 15 times a second.

login.body: Host facts, health and disk use printed once when someone logs in, with sample data so it runs anywhere.

steps.text: Install PowerShell 7 on the server if it is not there yet (Microsoft publishes packages for each distribution; on Ubuntu the snap is the quickest), then start it with `pwsh`.
In pwsh, install the module for your account.
Download the script into `~/bin` (it is the full program above; Copy on its panel works too), and run it once with `-Sample` to see the layout.
Show it when someone logs in over SSH. With pwsh as the login shell, add this to `~/.config/powershell/Microsoft.PowerShell_profile.ps1`; with bash, add the second block to the end of `~/.profile`.

code.label: ~/.profile (bash)
code.text:
case $- in
    *i*) if [ -n "$SSH_TTY" ] && command -v pwsh >/dev/null; then
             pwsh -NoLogo -NoProfile -File ~/bin/Example-LoginOverview.ps1
         fi ;;
esac

use.title: Run the full program
use.label: .NET 8 and later
use.install:
dotnet new console -n ConsoleMonsterDemo
cd ConsoleMonsterDemo
dotnet add package ConsoleMonster.Hosting
dotnet add package ConsoleMonster.Extensions.Logging
dotnet add package Microsoft.Extensions.Hosting
dotnet add package System.CommandLine
# Replace Program.cs with the full program above.
dotnet run -- hosting 12
